name: Robonaut 1
maker: NASA Johnson Space Center with DARPA
def: NASA's first dexterous humanoid torso, built with DARPA to test whether a teleoperated robot could handle astronaut tools and handrails.
body: Robonaut 1 paired two arms and five fingered hands with a stereo camera head on a torso sized to an astronaut's work envelope, and was driven through telepresence gloves and a head mounted display. Two units, R1A and R1B, were tested with a zero gravity leg that grips handrail sockets, on a Segway based Robotic Mobility Platform in 2003 and on the four wheeled Centaur 1 chassis in 2006. None flew in space, but its hands and control software led directly to Robonaut 2.
facts: First NASA humanoid built to use the same tools as astronauts
Tested on Segway based and four wheeled Centaur mobility platforms
specs: Electric brushless motors with tendon driven fingers
Stereo camera head with position, force and tactile sensing through the arms and hands
Telepresence operation with some autonomous grasping
